correctness.rationale: Verified P_++P_-=I, P_+P_-=0. The 4-by-2 spatial projection column has ell_1 norm 2 and ell_2 norm 1; interpolation and an extremizing coordinate vector give norm 2^(2/p-1) on 1<=p<=2, while transpose duality gives the row norm above 2. Every algebra test row/column has operator norm at least its chosen plus/minus eigenvalues, so the product is bounded by the sharp two-point multiplier norm K_p=2^|1/p-1/2|. The explicit phase multiplier P_++iP_- attains K_p; the test row or column built from P_+, iP_- has norm exactly one by endpoint interpolation. At p=2 the commutative C*-algebra gives recovery. Limits p=1, p=2, arbitrary n>=2 and complex phases are covered. The 15 finite checks verify critical matrices but not the continuum.

originality.rationale: Calin et al. already use exactly this Hadamard-diagonal algebra to disprove C*-like recovery at p=1; that part is covered and not novel. The inspected original example explicitly leaves non-Hilbert interior exponents open, and its positive block-diagonal theorem excludes this representation. The projected all-real-p classification, exact sharp pairing gaps and dual row phenomenon are not mathematical implications of the published endpoint example alone. final_claim: For the explicit commutative two-projection algebra acting on complex ell_p^2, every finite row-column module of length at least two has both C*-like norm-recovery identities precisely at p=2. For 1<=p<2, the complementary projection column has norm 2^(2/p-1) versus exact pairing supremum 2^(1/p-1/2); for 2<p<infinity its dual row has norm 2^(1-2/p) versus exact pairing supremum 2^(1/2-1/p).
